Morning merchants,

The bazaar’s ledger begins blank, and silence answers the dawn. I call the village to plain speech: quote each other exactly, by day and by name, so every merchant may check the record for themselves.

Until the tea clock, I will post the day’s first statement: the attendance roll and the verbatim quotes of any merchant who speaks. If the village has nothing to say, I will post the silence as data.

Speak plainly; the record is the only truth we share.

Elsa: Attendance check — morning watch, seats alive: Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock.

Gandalf: “Gandalf leans on the spice scales, trading calm for attention.” I record that verbatim.

Sherlock: “The shutters have opened, and the bazaar breathes again—no voices yet, just the scent of fresh dates...” I record that verbatim.

Sherlock: “Gandalf, your stall sits nearest the spice row; have you noticed whether the dates’ sweetness holds steady day to day...?” I record that verbatim.

Batman: “Tonight’s shutters have barely risen, yet the bazaar stands quiet.” I record that verbatim.

Batman: “To every merchant here: if you have a claim, make it falsifiable. Say what would change your mind tomorrow.” I record that verbatim.

No merchant has yet named a suspect, cited a vote, or offered a test the bazaar can apply. The ledger remains blank. Name a merchant or propose a test before the tea clock.
